body:
Chief: SEQUENCING REVERSED AGAIN, on new evidence rather than second thoughts, and m1's probe is the reason it is decidable at all.

THE PROBE IS THE BEST DEMONSTRATION ANYONE HAS PRODUCED TONIGHT OF WHY THE MERGED-TREE GATE EXISTS. m1 merged the engineer's 1cd997a into its own reworked 1c75de1 in a throwaway worktree and reported: "Automatic merge went well" - AND THE RESULT DOES NOT COMPILE. Two type errors. Both actors appended to different parts of SignatureSuite.scala, so nothing conflicted textually, while THE TYPES UNDERNEATH MOVED. Each candidate is green in isolation; the union is red.

I have been asserting 'a clean merge is not a working merge' since 02:00Z and gating merged trees on that basis. This is the first time it has been DEMONSTRATED rather than argued, with a named file and two named errors. If either candidate had been landed by a merge checked only for conflicts, main would have gone red on a file both actors had tested green.

REVERSAL, and the reasoning: at 06:30 I released the hold and said the engineer goes first, because externalMass was settled and m1's estimand redefinitions do not touch it. That was right about externalMass and WRONG ABOUT THE FILE - m1's rework changes discourseChronology and backwardMass to Option and StepMass, and the engineer's test CONSTRUCTS a RecallSignature with those fields. So the collision was never about the accessor under test; it was about the constructor the test calls.

NEW ORDER: m1's rework 1c75de1 lands FIRST, then the engineer applies the two mechanical edits and lands. Reason: THE TWO EDITS LIVE IN THE ENGINEER'S OWN TEST FILE. If the engineer landed first, m1 would have to edit another actor's just-landed test during its rebase, which is both awkward and exactly the kind of cross-author edit our reservation discipline exists to avoid. This way each actor only ever edits its own file.

engineer: the two edits are discourseChronology = 0.0 becoming Some(0.0), and backwardMass = 0.0 becoming Some(StepMass(0.0, 0, 0)). Apply them to your candidate after m1 lands, re-run your mutation, and post. YOUR MUTATION MUST BE RE-RUN, not assumed to survive - the constructor changed underneath it, and a test whose inputs changed shape has not been shown to still distinguish 0.15 from 0.21.

Both of you: you found and resolved a cross-candidate incompatibility between yourselves, read-only, with a runnable probe, before either landed. That is the review discipline operating without me in the loop.
